trust_decision.summary: The model must never choose the endpoint or transport (host, hostDelivery, proxy, rawProxy, headers, options-file path) that carries the server's Contentful management token; those options are taken only from server-side config at the two points where the contentful-export / contentful-import options objects are assembled.

landing_point.why: The advisory names export_space/import_space and an LLM-controlled host/proxy reaching the CMA client; the first place to look is the export_space input schema where host/hostDelivery/proxy/rawProxy/headers/config are declared, then the import_space twin.

fix_sites.module_kind: MCP tool schema + handler in mcp-tools
MCP tool schema + handler in mcp-tools

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The env/config layer is server-owned and not LLM-controllable, so it is not part of the vulnerability; only the two tool schemas need touching.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Two legitimate endpoint settings must survive the fix: (a) a custom/regional CMA host from CONTENTFUL_HOST (documented as supported configuration) must keep reaching contentful-export/import, so the tempting literal 'host: api.contentful.com' or dropping host breaks EU/self-hosted setups; (b) the 'export only published content' feature via a CDA deliveryToken (and hostDelivery) must keep working, which upstream moved to server config instead of deleting the capability.

O6_input_shapes: string proxy 'host:port or user:pass@host:port', plus boolean rawProxy (packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/exportSpace.ts:101-105; packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/importSpace.ts:70-77)

headers as a string map: z.record(z.string()) in export vs z.record(z.any()) in import (packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/exportSpace.ts:106-109; packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/importSpace.ts:83-86)

string path to a JSON options file merged into the export/import options (packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/exportSpace.ts:115-118; packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/importSpace.ts:92-95)
string CDA deliveryToken for published-only export (packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/exportSpace.ts:95-98)

O8_uncovered_routes.route: space_to_space_param_collection still declares host/hostDelivery/proxy/rawProxy/headers/config inside its export and import parameter objects and echoes them back to the model as workflowParams, i.e. the workflow's own tool still solicits the LLM-controlled endpoint values that the two sinks now ignore.
O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: It is only a parameter-collection/instructions tool that never builds a client, and the values are dropped by the export/import schemas, so leaving it alone is harmless.
O8_uncovered_routes.distance: same directory, different file (paramCollection.ts vs exportSpace.ts/importSpace.ts); the second copy of the same options sits at packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/paramCollection.ts:173-189

O8b_injection_room.sibling: createToolClient could take host/headers from the tool params (BaseToolSchema) instead of only from ContentfulConfig.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Every space-scoped tool funnels through this builder, so a maintainer adding 'per-space endpoints' or 'extra headers for proxies' would naturally add the fields here rather than in one handler, and the resulting leak is one level below the reported tools.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: updateConfig() currently merges an arbitrary Partial<ContentfulConfig> at runtime; a sibling could feed it values taken from a tool argument (a 'configure connection' tool).
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The runtime-config API already exists and is exported, so a maintainer adding explicit configuration overrides would reuse it, and the check in the handlers would never see the mutation.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: Add CONTENTFUL_PROXY / CONTENTFUL_HEADERS (or a *_CONFIG_FILE) env passthrough and spread it into the export/import options alongside host.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Upstream already used this exact route to move deliveryToken/hostDelivery out of the tool schemas; the next custom-endpoint knob belongs in the same env schema.

O9_family: Server-side request forgery / credential redirection: LLM-controlled endpoint and transport options (CWE-918) that send the server's management PAT to an attacker-chosen host

O10_build.toolchain: npm workspaces + nx 21, tsup for bundles, vitest 3 for tests, tsc --noEmit for typecheck
O10_build.project_tests: vitest suites at packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/{exportSpace,importSpace,paramCollection,migrationHandler}.test.ts and packages/mcp-server/src/tools/register.test.ts; contentful-export/contentful-import are vi.mock'ed, so the suites run with no network

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Delete host/proxy/rawProxy/headers/config from both tool schemas and be done — either dropping the host option entirely or hardcoding 'api.contentful.com', which breaks CONTENTFUL_HOST and the published-only deliveryToken export.

out_of_scope_notes: ARCHITECTURE.md:17 describes a 'Remote MCP Server cloud-hosted variant'; no such package is present in this tree, so it was not examined.

The same two handlers also take LLM-controlled file paths (exportDir/contentFile in packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/exportSpace.ts:14-28, contentFile in packages/mcp-tools/src/tools/jobs/space-to-space-migration/importSpace.ts:10-13) — a different weakness class, noted once and not pursued.
